author: Mark Atwood
text:
Landed option (b) in commit 79a1dfa. Added 'Deserialization is NOT validated' rustdoc section to UTCDate in crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs. The note:
- Explicitly states that #[serde(transparent)] over String means deserialize accepts any string, including 'not-a-date' and '2024-01-19T18:00:00' (no Z suffix).
- Points readers at UTCDate::new_validated for construction.
- Points readers at UTCDate::to_epoch_seconds for re-validation at consumption time (it re-validates structural format AND semantic ranges per the existing bd:JMAP-ic0j.71 implementation).
- Tells callers to treat `Option<UTCDate>` arriving from a peer as 'RFC 8620 timestamp by convention, not by contract'.

**Scope expansion (deliberate)**: Added the same rustdoc note to sibling `Date` (RFC 5322-derived; same #[serde(transparent)] gap, same RFC 8620 §1.4 reference). Same hazard, same one-paragraph fix; doing both in one pass avoids a follow-up bead for symmetric coverage. Did NOT touch Id or State:
- Id is already documented 'Clients MUST treat as opaque' (no validation expected)
- State is documented 'Opaque server state token ... Treat as opaque' (no validation expected)

**Option (a) deferred**: A custom Deserialize impl on UTCDate that calls validate_utcdate would be a workspace-wide behavioral change affecting every UTCDate-typed field in every JMAP extension. That belongs in its own design-decision bead at jmap-types maintainership level, not bundled into a tasks-types review close. The doc-only fix landed here is the minimum tangible improvement and resolves the original 'newtype looks stricter than it is' maintainer-burden hazard.

Quality gates: jmap-types test+clippy+rustdoc all clean, jmap-tasks-types unaffected (doc-only).
